regime: Oil-shock watch in a quiet holiday session: oil up again, gold soft, silver firm
takeaway: With US stock and bond markets shut for Thanksgiving, Brent settled at $96.57, up about 2% on the day and about 8% in three sessions on Gulf supply fears, which keeps the oil-shock check in view. Gold slipped about 0.6% to near $3,566 as Fed hike expectations held, while silver edged up, pulling the gold/silver ratio down to about 86 and easing the silver-under-stress check a little. The yen barely moved after slightly soft Tokyo inflation data, so there is no sign of a carry unwind; stock funds, yields and the VIX still show Wednesday's closes until trading resumes Friday.
